title: Employee-relations investigation and evidence handling - historical case pattern
summary: Several restricted employee-relations cases show a recurring historical investigation pattern: receive a complaint/incident, gather multiple accounts and objective records, give the employee an opportunity to respond, escalate serious matters, document participants/evidence, use interim action where necessary, and update the case when new evidence emerges.

claims.claim: A 2013 safety/vehicle case documents management comparing an employee account with a written inspection report, garage observations and later information from external/technical contacts before treating the matter as settled.

evidence.page_or_section: restricted 2013 vehicle/safety investigation record - generalized evidence sequence

claims.claim: The same case records a three-day suspension as 'pending further investigation' and explicitly adds later information that was unavailable when the interim decision was made, demonstrating separation between interim action and final evidentiary assessment.

evidence.page_or_section: restricted 2013 investigation record - procedural language only
evidence.note: This is a historical example, not a current mandatory suspension rule.

claims.claim: A separate 2013 customer-conduct case shows a complaint escalating from area management to Human Resources and executive leadership, followed by an employee interview/opportunity to respond, management discussion, and a leadership decision.

evidence.page_or_section: restricted 2013 customer-conduct case - generalized workflow only
evidence.note: Complaint allegations are not promoted as facts.

claims.claim: A 2014 workplace-conflict case shows HR being brought into an already tense meeting, directing participants/managers to document the meeting, changing communication routing to reduce direct conflict, and ensuring senior leadership was made aware.

A 2019 workplace-environment conversation documents HR asking whether the employee had followed the chain of command before escalating and considering department-wide training as a response to recurring communication/customer-service concerns.

Taken together, these cases support a process candidate that investigation records should distinguish allegation, source evidence, employee response, interim action, later evidence and final decision rather than collapsing them into one narrative.

evidence.note: Promotion to canonical current process requires present-day confirmation.

trigger: Serious complaint, safety concern, workplace conflict or possible policy violation requires fact-finding before final corrective action.
prerequisites: Identify applicable current policy and authorized decision-makers.
steps: Open a restricted case and separate the allegation from established facts.
Obtain the employee's response and relevant witness/manager accounts.
Escalate serious matters to the appropriate leadership/HR decision-maker.
If interim action is needed, label it as interim/pending investigation rather than a final finding.
Add later evidence to the existing case and reassess earlier conclusions when necessary.
Document the final decision and evidence relied upon.
decisions: Whether evidence is sufficient or additional fact-finding is needed.
Whether new evidence changes the assessment.
Whether corrective action, training, mediation/routing change or no action is appropriate.
controls: Do not treat allegations as findings.
Record contradictory/exculpatory evidence, not only inculpatory evidence.
Preserve the distinction between interim and final action.
Give the employee a meaningful opportunity to respond where the process permits.
Document participants, evidence provenance and later evidence additions.
Keep case facts restricted and only promote generalized process knowledge.
unresolved_questions: What is the current standardized employee-relations investigation checklist, case status model and approval chain?
When is paid/unpaid suspension pending investigation permitted today, and who must approve it?
Does current practice require discipline discussions to occur privately and prohibit disciplinary communication over shared radio/communications channels?
What current documentation is required when a complaint is resolved through training/mediation rather than discipline?
automation_candidates: Employee-relations case workflow with separate allegation/evidence/response/finding/interim-action fields.
Evidence timeline that preserves when each fact became known and supports reassessment after later evidence.
Required employee-response checkpoint before final discipline unless a documented exception applies.
Case-level audit log for who reviewed evidence and approved interim/final action.

provenance.notes: Names, allegations and individual findings excluded.
